helpful: The provisioned application.txt (full 38-page text) made the jurisdictional and merits posture legible without any retrieval.
The frozen ladder fields in context.json made the three increment claims unambiguous to state from.
The interim statpack section clears the 50-resolved floor for Term 2026, so a scored baseline existed (31/296 pooled over Terms 2024-2025).
gaps: fedcourts query with --include-applications still ranks time-extension grants ahead of substantive ones; a substantive-only filter would make the interim priors surface useful.

The statpack's interim section publishes no grant rate conditioned on response-requested or on applicant class (government vs private, federal vs state court below); for a private applicant with a response requested those cuts dominate the pooled rate.
fedcourts corpus-info does not work through the cell's corpus service, so the corpus-freshness norm cannot be met from a cell.
CourtListener carries no SCOTUS application dockets, so the MCP server had nothing on this case; the docket state had to come from a web fetch of supremecourt.gov.
notes: The WebSearch tool's summary layer fabricated a disposition for this application (dated before the application was filed). A cell relying on that summary rather than the docket page would have mis-flagged the cell as already decided. Treat WebSearch summaries as untrusted and verify against primary sources.
